title: How to Find a Home That Brings Your Family Closer This Mid-Autumn
summary: This Mid-Autumn, find a Singapore home that brings your family closer. Get a complimentary Family Move Plan with Ohmyhome.
body_text: Last Updated on August 14, 2026 by Yolly Del Prado Mid-Autumn is a time for reunion and reflection. It is also a meaningful moment to consider whether your current address still supports the way your family lives, grows and stays connected. Whether you’re purchasing your first property or looking for your next one, Ohmyhome makes it simple to buy a home in Singapore . This Mid-Autumn, start your search for a new home with us and find an address that fits your family’s future. Begin With the People You Want Around the Table As your family gathers this Mid-Autumn, think about how your household may change by the time you celebrate together in the years ahead. Children grow, parents get older and working arrangements can change. You do not need to predict every possibility, but it helps to consider who your next home may need to support. Ask yourselves: Who will live in the home now? Could a parent or relative move in later? How much privacy does each person need? Will young children eventually need separate rooms? Does anyone regularly work or study from home? Would an older family member need step-free access? How long do you hope to stay in the property? Your answers can give you a clearer idea of the space and layout your family may need, both for everyday life and future gatherings. A larger home can certainly help, but size alone does not determine how well a home works. A practical layout may serve your family better than additional floor area that is difficult to use. I Lived in a Multi-Generational Home and Here’s What It’s Really Like Think About the Journey Home Mid-Autumn may bring everyone home for one special evening, but the location of your home can shape how easily your family comes together throughout the rest of the year. Travelling across Singapore for an annual reunion may feel manageable. Making the same journey several times a week for childcare, caregiving or family meals can feel very different. When comparing neighbourhoods, consider: Travelling time to parents and close relatives Routes to workplaces and schools Access to MRT stations and bus services Nearby childcare, healthcare and daily necessities Whether older relatives can reach the home comfortably The safety and convenience of walking routes Future developments that may affect the area You may find that living closer to family is more useful than having an additional facility or a slightly larger home elsewhere. Instead of comparing locations only by their distance on a map, think about how much time each one could give back to your family. Plan for Everyday Life As Well As Celebrations It is natural to picture everyone gathering in the living or dining area during Mid-Autumn. However, your next home also needs to work on regular days, when everyone is following a different routine. Imagine a typical weekday in the home: Is there enough storage for everyday belongings? Can someone work while another person watches television? Is the kitchen suitable for how often your family cooks? Do the bedrooms provide enough privacy? Is there space for children to play or study? Would the home be easy to maintain? Can the layout adapt as your family’s needs change? Look at the floor plan before arranging a viewing and consider how everyone would move through the space. A home can look spacious in photographs but offer little usable room once furniture and storage are considered. On the other hand, a smaller home with a practical layout may feel much more comfortable. Create Your Family Move Plan Once you understand what your family needs, bring the practical and financial details together. Your Family Move Plan should include: Your estimated purchasing budget Available cash and CPF funds Financing options and monthly commitments Preferred property type Suitable neighbourhoods Required floor area and layout Proximity to family, schools and workplaces Accessibility requirements Expected renovation or repair costs Your preferred purchasing timeline How long you intend to live in or own the home Then sort your requirements into three groups: Must-haves: Things your family genuinely needs from the home Strong preferences: Important features with some room for compromise Bonuses: Features you would enjoy but can live without This becomes especially helpful when two homes appeal to you for different reasons. Instead of choosing based on the stronger first impression, you can return to the priorities your family agreed on together. Plan My Family’s Next Move Shortlist Homes Without Losing Sight of Your Priorities Searching for a family home in Singapore can become overwhelming. There will always be another listing, neighbourhood or property type to compare. Instead of reviewing every available home, focus first on properties that meet your family’s most important requirements. For each home, compare: Asking price and recent transactions Remaining lease or tenure Floor plan and usable space Property condition Likely renovation or repair costs Monthly maintenance charges, where applicable Transport and daily amenities Proximity to schools, workplaces and relatives Noise, privacy and surroundings Planned developments in the area An attractive listing may still be unsuitable if it stretches your budget, adds too much travelling time or requires more renovation than expected. Ohmyhome’s technology can help match your requirements with suitable homes, allowing you to focus on properties that are more likely to fit your family. Simply submit your preferences or browse homes for sale across Singapore to begin your search. During the Viewing, Picture Your Family Living There When viewing a home, start by imagining the next Mid-Autumn taking place there. Where would everyone sit? Could older relatives move around comfortably? Would children have somewhere safe to play? These questions can help you understand whether the shared spaces would support the moments you hope to enjoy together. Then consider how the home would work on an ordinary day. Where would school bags, groceries and laundry go? Would family members have enough room to work, rest and spend time together without constantly getting in one another’s way? Once you have considered how the home might feel, inspect its practical condition: Natural light and ventilation Noise from neighbours, roads or nearby facilities Privacy from surrounding units Available storage The condition of walls, flooring and built-in fixtures Signs of leaks, moisture or other maintenance issues The condition of shared areas and facilities Mobile reception and the location of electrical points The walking route to the nearest transport stop The overall environment of the neighbourhood Take photographs and notes, where permitted, immediately after each viewing. After several appointments, the details of different homes can easily begin to blur together. One useful question to ask after every viewing is: “What would become easier for our family if we lived here, and what might become harder?” This helps you judge the home by how it would affect family life, not only by how attractive it appears during the viewing. Book a Property Viewing Look Beyond the Asking Price Before Making An Offer Once you find a suitable property, avoid deciding how much to offer based only on the asking price. Consider: Recent transactions for comparable homes The unit’s floor level, facing and condition Renovation and immediate repair costs Competing listings in the development or area Current buyer interest Your financing and comfortable spending limit The seller’s preferred completion timeline Whether the home still meets your agreed must-haves Remember to consider the total cost of the move. A lower-priced home may require substantial renovation, while a more expensive home in a convenient location may reduce transport or caregiving demands for several family members. The aim is not simply to secure the home. It is to make a decision your family can remain comfortable with after the excitement settles. Get Help With My Family’s Move Prepare for the Move Before Getting the Keys After your offer is accepted, there are still several steps to complete. Depending on the property type, these may include: Confirming your financing arrangements Preparing and reviewing the required documents Monitoring transaction deadlines Coordinating with the seller Planning renovation or repair work Arranging utilities and moving services Preparing for completion and handover This is also a good time to prepare your family for the practical changes ahead. Children may need to become familiar with a new route to school, while older relatives may need help learning how to reach the new home. Planning these details early can help everyone settle in more comfortably. Make Room for More Than One Evening Together Mid-Autumn reminds us how meaningful it is to gather. But closeness is also built on ordinary days: sharing dinner after work, helping with the children or dropping by your parents’ home without needing to plan weeks ahead. Your next home does not have to be the biggest or most impressive property you view. It should be the one that best supports the way your family hopes to live and stay connected. Ohmyhome’s Super Agents can help you create a complimentary Family Move Plan, shortlist suitable homes and navigate the buying process from your first search to getting the keys. Because the right home is not only where your family reunites for Mid-Autumn. It is where everyday moments together can happen more naturally, for many years to come. This Mid-Autumn, start planning a move that brings the people who matter closer. Message us on WhatsApp , or browse homes for sale across Singapore . Frequently Asked Questions What type of home suits a multigenerational family in Singapore? An HDB 3Gen flat is the most purpose-built option, as its four bedrooms and three bathrooms give parents and married children more privacy under one roof. However, a larger resale HDB flat may offer more location choices, while a dual-key condo can provide greater separation between generations. Whichever you consider, compare the layout, accessibility and monthly costs, not just the floor area. Is Mid-Autumn a good time to buy a home in Singapore? Mid-Autumn can be a meaningful time to begin your home search, especially if family gatherings have prompted conversations about space, location or living closer together. However, the festival itself should not determine when you buy. Your finances, housing needs and readiness to commit should still guide the timing of your move. Do I need a bigger home to host family gatherings comfortably? No, a bigger home is not always necessary for comfortable family gatherings. A practical layout can matter more than total floor area. Look for connected living and dining spaces, enough room to move around and a layout that can accommodate additional seating without blocking walkways. Also consider whether older relatives can enter and use the home comfortably.

title: Ninja Raises the Standard for Home Water with the Launch of Ninja HydraSense™
summary: Ninja Raises the Standard for Home Water with the Launch of Ninja HydraSense™. The latest on SharkNinja innovations—press releases, product launches, media kits, images, and press contacts.
body_text: The new intelligent water filtration system removes up to 99% and 80+ contaminants—including PFAS, lead, pesticides, carcinogens, microplastics, and pharmaceuticals; all while preserving the minerals that make water taste great. NEEDHAM, Mass.–(BUSINESS WIRE)– SharkNinja, Inc. (NYSE: SN), a leading global product design and technology company, today introduced Ninja HydraSense, an intelligent water filtration system built to raise expectations for what home water filtration should deliver. Consumers shouldn’t have to wonder what’s in their water, or choose between cleaner water and convenience, and with Ninja HydraSense, they no longer have to. Ninja HydraSense The breakthrough is in the balance. While some premium systems may strip water of the minerals and electrolytes that contribute to its flavor, Ninja HydraSense preserves calcium, magnesium, and potassium for smooth, refreshing water that tastes the way it should. The result is a premium-quality water experience, without the plastic waste of bottled water. Powered by Ninja’s new Precision Pressure Technology, Ninja HydraSense removes up to 99% and more than 80 contaminants1. The leading pitcher filters trap only around 8 contaminants, and some more comprehensive filters only capture 33.2 The system is certified to NSF 42, 53 and 401 standards and removes up to 10 times more contaminants than the leading filter3. “We set out to raise the standard for filtered water at home,” said Kaitlyn Hebert, Global Chief Marketing Officer at SharkNinja. “Ninja HydraSense was built with our mission of positively impacting people’s lives at its core. Clean, great-tasting water is something everyone deserves, and by bringing intelligent filtration and effortless ease of use together in one countertop system, we’re helping make cleaner water the standard, not a luxury.” Ninja HydraSense is also built for speed and simplicity. It dispenses water up to 6 times faster than the leading pitcher, making it easy to use filtered water throughout your day—not just for drinking, but also for brewing coffee and tea, cooking, filling water bottles, and even keeping pets hydrated. It also offers personalized hydration tracking and real-time filter monitoring based on personal usage. And with a 120-gallon filter life, there’s no plumbing and no installation required—just fill, filter, and go. Beyond performance, Ninja HydraSense is designed to help consumers cut down on single-use plastic. Every filter can replace up to 900 plastic bottles, giving households filtered water at home without the hassle of buying, carrying, or storing bottled water. Starting August 13, 2026, the Ninja HydraSense will be available at SharkNinja.com for $199.99 with additional replacement filters at $39.99. About SharkNinja SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market, and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world. title: Trade Finance for O'Hare-Area Importers: Faster Payment Cycles for Air Freight
summary: Air cargo importer financing Chicago: why fast air freight does not shorten the vendor payment gap, and how Chicago import financing covers it. Trade Finance fo
body_text: Trade Finance for O'Hare-Area Importers: Faster Payment Cycles for Air Freight Air freight is the answer to a timing problem, and air cargo importer financing in Chicago has to answer a different one. A component runs short, a customer moves a deadline up, a product launch cannot slip, so the shipment flies instead of sails. Under a week instead of a month. What surprises importers is that flying the goods does almost nothing to the payment gap. The vendor still wants paying before the shipment leaves. Your customer still pays on their own terms after it arrives. Air freight compresses the transit and leaves the cash cycle largely where it was, which is the gap Chicago import financing has to cover. Why O'Hare Sits at the Center of This O'Hare is one of the largest air cargo gateways in the world. It processes over two million metric tonnes of cargo worth more than $200 billion, ranking first by freight value among all airports in the Americas , served by more than 25 cargo carriers connecting Asia, Europe, and the Americas. That concentration is why the cargo corridor around the airport is dense with importers, freight forwarders, and distribution operations, and why Elk Grove Village trade finance is a recognisable need in its own right. If you are importing high-value or time-sensitive goods into the Midwest, this is where they land. Air freight costs more per shipment, and it costs it sooner Air freight can run five to fifteen times the per-kilo cost of ocean. That changes the shape of the cash outlay, not just the size. You are paying a premium rate on freight at roughly the same moment you are paying the vendor, and both land well before your customer pays you. A shipment that flies is a bigger cash event compressed into a shorter window, which is why air freight importer funding gets sized differently from ocean financing. Urgency removes your negotiating room The reason you are flying the goods is usually that something is already tight. That is a poor position from which to ask a vendor for longer terms or a smaller deposit. Chicago import financing ends up replacing the terms you did not have room to negotiate. By the numbers Air cargo importer financing in Chicago, by the numbers 2M+ metric tonnes of cargo through O'Hare $200B+ in freight value, first in the Americas 48% of firms sourced at least some inputs from outside the US (2024) More than 4 in 10 firms report tariff- related costs as a financial challenge Source: Chicago Department of Aviation; Federal Reserve Banks, 2026 Report on Employer Firms ![what air freight does and does not compress](https://images.ctfassets.net/vkoe68wv76dt/4xkM7nWD0eBZUs1g4VnSOG/b356dbf6e4ed2e6a6838aa55e7a6c16c/infographic-1-air-vs-ocean) Where the Cash Actually Goes Three outflows stack up on an air shipment, and they arrive close together, which is what sets air cargo importer financing in Chicago apart from a standard import facility. The vendor payment before departure Many overseas vendors expect payment, or a deposit, before goods are released to the carrier. On an air shipment the timeline is short enough that this often means paying within days of the order, with little room to stage the payment. Freight and handling at a premium Air freight, fuel surcharges, and handling cost significantly more than the ocean equivalent. For a high-value or urgent shipment that premium can be worth paying, and it still comes out of the same working capital. Customer terms that do not flex Your buyer's payment terms were set in a contract, and they rarely shorten because you chose to expedite. Flying the shipment moved your costs earlier without moving your revenue earlier, which is a working capital squeeze by definition. Funding the Gap Without Slowing Down The tools behind air freight importer funding need to move at the speed of the shipment. Vendor Financing Vendor Financing pays your overseas vendor directly, so the goods are released and loaded without draining your account. You repay within an agreed window, typically up to ninety days, and pricing is a flat fee on the invoice, usually 1% to 3% per month, charged only on what you draw and only while it stays outstanding. For an importer whose whole reason for flying is speed, having the vendor paid quickly is the point, and it is the core of most Elk Grove Village trade finance arrangements. A Line of Credit A Line of Credit suits importers who expedite regularly. Because it is revolving, the facility is already in place when the next urgent shipment appears, which matters when the decision to fly gets made in a single afternoon. That readiness is the main argument for arranging air freight importer funding before you need it. That structure differs from a bank loan , where you take the full amount up front whether you need it yet or not. Planning for the expedite you know is coming If you fly several shipments a year, the pattern is predictable even when the individual shipment is not. Sizing a facility around that pattern in a quiet month beats arranging financing during a scramble. Our guide to small business financing options covers how the alternatives compare. The orders are booked. Make sure your cash can keep up. Drip Capital funds the materials, payroll, and inventory that sit between a signed order and a paid invoice. Talk to Drip Capital → $9B+ trade financed • 11,000+ businesses served • 100+ countries What to Have Ready Before You Need It Air freight decisions happen fast, so the paperwork should already exist. Keep the vendor's invoice or pro forma and your business formation documents accessible. Importers who arrange Chicago import financing before the urgent shipment arrives get to use it on the shipment that actually matters. How Drip Capital Helps Air Freight Importers Drip Capital pays your vendor directly, so a release-before-payment demand does not force you to choose between the shipment and the rest of the month. Repayment falls within an agreed window, typically up to ninety days, and the cost is a flat fee on the invoice rather than something you discover later. It is collateral-free, and no personal guarantee is required. Vendor Financing through Drip Capital requires a minimum of two years in business. Frequently Asked Questions If air freight is faster than ocean, why would an importer need financing? Because transit was never the long part, which is the premise behind air cargo importer financing in Chicago . The vendor is paid before departure and the customer pays on their own contracted terms after delivery, so the cash gap remains even when the flight is short. Air freight also costs more per shipment, which makes the outlay larger. Is financing fast enough to use on an expedited air shipment? It depends on whether the facility already exists. Importers who expedite regularly benefit from arranging financing in advance rather than mid-scramble, so the facility is ready when the next urgent shipment appears. Does Drip Capital finance the freight cost or just the goods? Vendor Financing pays your vendor for the goods. Do I need to be near O'Hare to qualify? No. Location does not drive eligibility for US businesses, so Elk Grove Village trade finance works the same way regardless of where you are based. What matters is a confirmed order, a reliable vendor, and meeting the minimum of two years in business.

body_text: Axalta Shareholders Approve Proposed Merger of Equals with AkzoNobel August 05, 2026 10:35 am EDT Download as PDF PHILADELPHIA, Aug. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Axalta Coating Systems Ltd. (NYSE: AXTA) today announced that its shareholders overwhelmingly voted to approve its previously announced all-stock merger of equals (the “Merger”) with Akzo Nobel N.V. (“AkzoNobel”) at the Company’s Special General Meeting of Shareholders held earlier today. AkzoNobel also held its Extraordinary General Meeting today, where AkzoNobel shareholders voted to approve the Merger. “We appreciate the strong support we have received for our merger of equals with AkzoNobel and we are excited about the opportunity to deliver significant value to shareholders, customers and employees,” said Chris Villavarayan, Chief Executive Officer of Axalta. “Building on our record second quarter, we are excited to embark on our next phase with real momentum in the business. Our teams are working diligently to advance integration planning and remain focused on bringing together two highly complementary businesses to capture the full value of this combination from day one.” “Today’s approval marks an important milestone toward creating a premier global coatings company,” said Rakesh Sachdev, Chair of the Axalta Board of Directors. “The resounding support reaffirms our conviction that combining Axalta and AkzoNobel will create a differentiated industry leader with broad capabilities, world-class innovation and an even stronger platform for growth and value creation. I look forward to working with our combined team to deliver on the promise of this combination.” Completion of the Merger remains subject to receipt of required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. Subject to the satisfaction of these conditions, the companies continue to expect the Merger to be completed in late 2026 to early 2027. The final voting results, as certified by an independent inspector of election, will be filed as a Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. From light vehicles, commercial vehicles and refinish applications to electric motors, building facades and other industrial applications, our coatings are designed to prevent corrosion, increase productivity and enhance durability. title: The Pomodoro Technique for Teams: Syncing Focus Sprints Together
summary: Discover how Pomodoro sprints enhance team focus and reduce stress! Set clear goals, sync rhythms, and track outcomes effectively.
body_text: The core: what a team Pomodoro sprint looks like Pomodoro uses short, timed sprints. Everyone starts and stops together. That shared rhythm reduces friction and context switches. Choose a clear, small goal for the next sprint. Work for 25 minutes with zero interruptions. Stop. Take a five‑minute break away from screens. Repeat three or four times, then take a longer break. We finish more and stress less when we pause before the mind begs for it. Set shared rules for team focus sprints Agree on basics: duration, signals, channels, and what counts as urgent. Keep the rules visible and short. Duration: 25 minutes work, five minutes rest. Adjust only after one week of use. Signals: One sound to start. One sound to stop. Headphones mean “do not disturb.” Channels: Mute chat during sprints. Post updates in breaks only. Urgent path: One escalations channel. One owner per day. Want a quick start? Draft a one‑page agreement and review it in ten minutes. Draft a concise Team Pomodoro Agreement for a hybrid product team. Include: Sprint length, break rules, mute policy, interruption triage, urgent channel, daily owner, and end‑of‑day recap format. Keep it to 8 bullet points, plain language. Why rules matter Pomodoro works when everyone plays by the same rules. Clarity prevents slack pings and drive‑by requests mid‑sprint. Translate sprints into project and CRM workflows Break large work into sprint‑sized chunks. Tie each chunk to a visible outcome. Engineering: “Write tests for module A” fits one sprint. “Ship feature” does not. Design: “Sketch first three hero options” fits. “Redesign homepage” does not. Sales: “Call five stale MQLs” fits. “Close deal” does not. Support: “Clear ten tickets with the same tag” fits. “Reduce churn” does not. Make progress visible. Consider visualizing team sprints on a lightweight project tracker so everyone sees flow across the day. Sales teams or groups, often called sales pods, can link timers to CRM actions. Use triggers for auto‑tasks, reminders, or follow‑ups. See the playbook on automations every B2B sales team should set up to reduce manual legwork between sprints. For instance, if you are a sales manager, you could map four focused sprints to advance a set of leads in one day. Here’s a practical prompt you can use: Example: Map four 25‑minute sprints that move 20 leads from Prospected to Qualified in one day. Specify call batches, email templates, voicemail scripts, and CRM updates after each sprint. Return as a checklist. Design quick rituals that connect people without breaking flow Keep touchpoints brief and consistent. Pre‑sprint huddle (2 minutes): Each person states one outcome. Mid‑block pit stop (3 minutes): Surface blockers only. Post‑block recap (5 minutes): Share outcomes and next step. For formats that scale, explore guidance similar to Running Effective Meetings: Formats, Minutes, Notes, and Recaps with Ready Templates . Keep your own ritual tight and repeatable. Handle interruptions with a simple triage playbook Not all pings are equal. Route, defer, or act using one rule set. Life or revenue at risk? Break the sprint. Log the reason. High priority, not urgent? Park it for the next break. Everything else: Queue it for the next planning slot. Use canned replies to protect focus and set expectations. Draft five friendly canned replies that defer non‑urgent requests until the next break. Include versions for clients, executives, peers, and vendors. Keep each under 25 words. Remote or hybrid teams: make async Pomodoro work Synchronized starts can be challenging across different time zones. Use windows, not exact minutes. Pick two daily focus windows that overlap for most people. Inside each window, run three to four sprints. Post outcomes after each sprint in a single thread. Log interruptions with brief notes, or capture visible ones with a short screen recording if needed. Async posts keep everyone aligned without long calls. Measure what matters: outcomes, not minutes Time is a constraint, not the goal. Track results people care about. Work moved: Task cards moved to the Done column, tickets resolved, leads advanced. Quality: Fewer regressions, clearer deliverables, happier customers. Flow: Interruptions per sprint and their causes. Share a tiny scoreboard at day’s end. Celebrate the small wins. Tools that help without becoming the work Pick tools that connect tasks, docs, CRM, and meetings in one place. Apps like Routine, ClickUp, or Notion can tie tasks to outcomes and link them to customer records. Keep the tech simple and stable. For timing, a basic web timer works fine. Try an online option like a minimal Pomodoro timer you can run in any browser . Common pitfalls and how to fix them Meetings collide with sprints: Group meetings outside focus windows. Tasks are too big: Slice until one sprint yields a visible outcome. Breaks vanish: Enforce them. Rest fuels the next sprint. Chat creep: Post in breaks only. Use threads. Monotony: Rotate task types across sprints when possible. Examples across roles that you can copy tomorrow Design team: Sprint 1 sketches three hero ideas. Sprint 2 builds one wireframe. Sprint 3 tests copy on two variants. Sales pod: Sprint 1 calls five stale leads. Sprint 2 sends five custom videos. Sprint 3 logs outcomes and sets callbacks. Support queue: Sprint 1 clears ten billing tickets. Sprint 2 writes one saved reply for a common issue. Sprint 3 closes five technical tickets. Want to place these sprints on a simple visual? This guide on choosing the right project visualization for short cycles can help align timelines with focus blocks. FAQ What is a Pomodoro sprint? A Pomodoro sprint is a focused work session that lasts 25 minutes, followed by a 5-minute break. This cycle helps reduce context switching and maintains high productivity levels. How can I prevent interruptions during a Pomodoro sprint? Set clear rules such as muting chat channels and using visible signals like headphones to designate focus time. Establish an urgent path with one dedicated person to handle escalations during sprints. What should be included in a Team Pomodoro Agreement? A Team Pomodoro Agreement should clearly outline sprint durations, break policies, mute rules, interruption triage processes, escalation channels, and a way to recap each day’s work. How does Routine help with implementing Pomodoro technique in a team? Routine integrates tasks, documentation, CRM, and meetings, making it easy to connect sprints with outcomes and streamline workflows. Using Routine mitigates multitasking, reducing manual legwork and distraction during focus sprints. What is the risk of not adhering to set sprint rules? Ignoring sprint rules can lead to distractions, interruptions, and decreased productivity. Consistent adherence ensures that the team remains aligned, and progress remains visible, preventing the chaos of unproductive multitasking. How can remote teams effectively implement Pomodoro sprints? Remote teams should use overlapping focus windows to synchronize starts as much as possible, and employ asynchronous updates to maintain team alignment. This approach mitigates time zone challenges while maintaining a collective effort. What common pitfalls should teams avoid when adopting Pomodoro sprints? Avoid scheduling meetings during focus windows, letting breaks disappear, and setting tasks that are too large for a single sprint. These missteps can erode the effectiveness of sprints and reduce overall productivity. How do I measure success in Pomodoro sprints? Focus on outcomes rather than time spent. Track completed tasks, resolved issues, and improved quality, as effectiveness is defined by progress and results, not just hours worked.

title: Recovering Lost Commits with Git Reflog
summary: Recover lost Git commits with reflog: use git reflog to find orphaned commits, undo hard resets and rebases, and restore branches fast.
body_text: To recover a lost commit, run git reflog , copy the hash of the commit you want, and restore it with git checkout -b recovered <hash> . You meant HEAD~1 , typed HEAD~2 , and watched three hours of work drop out of git log . Those few seconds between hitting enter and remembering the reflog exists are the worst in Git. When you run git reset --hard , botch a rebase, or delete a branch, your commits are almost never destroyed: they’re just orphaned, and their hashes are still recorded in your reflog. This guide gives you the fast recovery recipe for the three scenarios that cause the panic, then the hard limits worth knowing so you don’t lose the work a second time. Every command below is copy-pasteable. Key Takeaways git reflog records every move of HEAD in your local repository (commit, checkout, reset, rebase, merge), so a “lost” commit is usually one git reset --hard <hash> away from being back. The safest recovery is git checkout -b recovered <hash> : rebuild the commit on a new branch and inspect it before touching your real branch. Reflog cannot recover uncommitted working-directory changes, because Git never recorded them in a ref in the first place. By default Git keeps reachable reflog entries for 90 days and unreachable ones for 30 days, so recover promptly and avoid running git gc until you have your commits back. The reflog is strictly local and never pushed, so it can rescue your own lost work but not a teammate’s unpushed commits. How does Git reflog work? Git’s reflog is a local log of every position your branch tips and other refs have held. Every commit, checkout, reset, rebase, and merge moves HEAD and gets logged. So when a commit becomes “lost” (meaning no branch or tag points to it anymore) it is only orphaned , not deleted, and its hash still sits in the reflog waiting to be re-attached. Run the command with no arguments to see the history of HEAD : git reflog b58145c HEAD@{0}: reset: moving to HEAD~2 dd7c37e HEAD@{1}: commit: one more commit b5b3286 HEAD@{2}: checkout: moving from main to feature b58145c HEAD@{3}: commit: very important commit Read each line as: short hash , the HEAD@{n} index (how many moves back that entry sits), and a description of the operation. In the output above, HEAD@{0} is the destructive reset that just happened, and HEAD@{1} ( dd7c37e ) is the commit it moved away from, the one you want back. Under the hood, git reflog show runs the same thing as git log -g --abbrev-commit --pretty=oneline , and it takes any ref, so git reflog show main gives you one branch’s history. Recover from an accidental hard reset A git reset --hard moves your branch pointer but leaves the old commit intact in the object store. Find it in the reflog, then re-point to it. The commit just before the reset is the one you lost, usually HEAD@{1} . git reflog # HEAD@{0}: reset: moving to HEAD~2 # HEAD@{1}: commit: one more commit <-- this hash git checkout -b recovered dd7c37e The safest recovery is to inspect before you overwrite: run git checkout -b recovered <hash> to rebuild the commit on a new branch, verify it with git log , and only then decide whether to move your real branch. Once you’re sure, you can jump the branch directly: git reset --hard dd7c37e # or: git reset --hard HEAD@{1} Double-jeopardy warning: git reset --hard discards any current uncommitted changes in your working tree. If your tree is dirty, git stash or use the new-branch route first. Otherwise the recovery command causes a second loss. Immediately after a reset you can also use git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD , because git reset records the branch’s previous tip in ORIG_HEAD before it moves. Undo a bad rebase A rebase rewrites history, and a mis-resolved conflict can silently drop commits. Reflog holds the pre-rebase tip. After a bad rebase, git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD snaps your branch back to where it started. But ORIG_HEAD is overwritten by the next reset, rebase, or merge, so if you’ve run another such command since, find the pre-rebase tip in git reflog instead. git reflog # HEAD@{0}: rebase (finish): returning to refs/heads/feature # HEAD@{1}: rebase (pick): one more commit # HEAD@{2}: rebase (start): checkout main # HEAD@{3}: checkout: moving from main to feature <-- pre-rebase tip git reset --hard HEAD@{ 3 } Look for the rebase (start) entry; the line just before it is your branch as it stood pre-rebase. If you only want specific commits the rebase dropped rather than undoing the whole thing, grab their hashes from the reflog and replay them: git cherry-pick < has h > Recover a deleted branch Deleting a branch removes the ref, not the commits. Its last commit still appears in the reflog of HEAD (from when you last checked it out), so find that hash and recreate the branch at it. git reflog # HEAD@{0}: checkout: moving from example-branch to main # HEAD@{1}: commit: very important commit <-- last commit on deleted branch git checkout -b example-branch b5b3286 # or HEAD@{1} git checkout -b <branch> <hash> recreates the branch pointing at the recovered commit, with its history intact. If you remember part of a commit message but not the hash, git log --oneline -g --grep='<fragment>' searches the reflog for it. ( git switch -c is the modern equivalent of checkout -b ; both work, and checkout is not deprecated.) What can’t Git reflog recover? Reflog can recover anything that moved HEAD or a branch tip (commits, resets, rebases, deleted branches), but it cannot recover uncommitted working-directory changes , because Git never recorded them in a ref in the first place. If a change was never committed, there is no ref update for the reflog to point back to, so searching the reflog for it will not turn anything up. Reflog CAN recover Reflog CANNOT recover Commits orphaned by reset --hard Uncommitted edits in the working tree Commits dropped by a bad rebase Staged-but-uncommitted changes Deleted local branches (recent) A teammate’s unpushed commits Your local view of a force-pushed remote Entries already expired and gc’d Three more constraints govern recovery: It’s local and temporary. The reflog lives only in your .git directory and is never pushed, so it rescues your own work but not a teammate’s unpushed commits. Entries expire. By default Git keeps reachable reflog entries for 90 days and unreachable ones for 30 days, via gc.reflogExpire and gc.reflogExpireUnreachable . Orphaned commits survive until expiry plus a garbage-collection pass, so recover promptly and avoid running git gc until you’re done. Recover onto a new branch first. Make git checkout -b recovered <hash> your default move so you can verify before altering a shared branch. And write descriptive commit messages: reflog shows them, so “Fix login bug” is far easier to spot than a vague one. Bonus (after a force-push): the remote server has no reflog you can read, but your local tracking ref does. To recover commits wiped from a remote by a force-push, check your local record with git reflog show origin/<branch> . The entry just before the force-push holds the old tip. Conclusion The reflog is Git’s local safety net, and it turns nearly every “I lost my work” moment into a two-command fix: read the log, re-point to the hash. The one thing it can’t rescue is work you never committed, so the durable lesson is to commit early and often, which guarantees there’s always a reflog entry to find. Next time the terminal makes your stomach drop, run git reflog before anything else. FAQs What is the difference between git reflog and git log? git log shows the commit history reachable from a branch tip, following parent pointers, so orphaned commits never appear in it. git reflog shows every position HEAD or a ref has occupied in your local repository — commits, checkouts, resets, rebases, and merges — including commits that no branch points to anymore. That is why reflog can find a commit after a hard reset when git log cannot: the commit is orphaned but its ref update is still logged. Does git reflog work after cloning a repository? No. The reflog is stored only in your local .git directory and is never pushed or fetched, so a fresh clone starts with an empty reflog covering only actions taken since you cloned. It cannot show HEAD movements from before the clone or reveal a teammate's local history. Reflog rescues your own lost work in your own repository; it is not a shared or remote-backed recovery tool. Can I recover a commit after git reflog entries have expired? Not through the reflog itself. By default reachable entries expire after 90 days and unreachable ones after 30 days, and once a garbage-collection pass prunes the orphaned objects they are truly gone. Before that, you can sometimes still find the hash with git fsck --lost-found, which lists dangling commits in the object store. The reliable move is to recover promptly and avoid running git gc until your commits are back. How do I find a lost commit if I don't know its hash? Search the reflog directly. Run git log --oneline -g --grep='fragment' to filter reflog entries by part of a commit message, or git reflog --date=relative to scan entries by time and spot the operation you want to undo. For orphaned commits with no reflog entry, git fsck --lost-found lists dangling commits you can inspect with git show before recovering onto a new branch with git checkout -b recovered <hash>.
